nav.label: Main
home.title: Home
page.soon.hint: Nothing to set up yet. Hearth discovers everything on its own.
auth.title: Open Hearth from the launcher
auth.body: This tab has no session. Use the Hearth entry in your application menu to open a signed-in window.
notfound.title: Page not found
home.customizeHint: Drag cards to reorder them, or use the arrow buttons. Hidden cards are listed below the grid.
home.saveFailed: The layout could not be saved. Changes apply to this page only.
card.gpu.sleeping: Asleep. Not read, so it can stay asleep and save power.
card.gpu.noUtil: Clock speed. Usage is not reported by this driver.
card.docker.name: Container
resources.title: Resources
resources.empty: No history for this range yet. Hearth records it while running; check back later.
apps.search: Search apps, services, processes or PID
apps.col.name: Name
apps.ioPartial: Some processes belong to another user and their disk activity cannot be read.
apps.footnote: CPU is a share of the whole machine. Memory of apps, services and containers is their cgroup's usage (shared memory counted once, file cache included); for single processes it is resident memory. Disk I/O is unknown (–) where neither the cgroup nor the processes can be read. Network use per app needs elevated privileges and is not shown.
confirm.affects: This affects {n} process(es). Unsaved work in them may be lost.
reason.otherUser: runs as {user}; Hearth acts only on your processes
reason.session: ending or pausing it would end or freeze your desktop session
reason.browser: this browser is showing Hearth; pausing it would freeze this page
reason.denied: not permitted (raising priority needs administrator rights)
reason.unauthorized: not authorized: the password dialog was cancelled or refused
reason.masked: masked: it cannot be started until it is unmasked
reason.noInstall: it has no [Install] section, so it cannot be enabled (it is started by other units)
reason.essential: marked Essential: the system cannot work without it
reason.protected: marked Protected by Debian: removing it would break the system
reason.required: Priority required: part of every Debian system
reason.manager: it is the package manager itself
reason.root: installed for all users; remove it with sudo
reason.pip: remove it with pip; Hearth will not override Debian's protection of the system Python
apps2.title: Applications
apps2.cannotClose: {name} cannot be closed from here: it is part of your desktop session or runs as another user.
svc.title: Services
svc.intro: Everything systemd runs, for the system and for you.
svc.criticalHint: Stopping or disabling this can break the system or your session.
svc.footnote: "At boot" is the unit file state (enabled, disabled, static: started only by other units, masked: cannot start). Memory is the unit's cgroup usage, file cache included; CPU is a share of the whole machine.
svc.done.disable: {name} will no longer start at boot.
svc.authHint: If a password dialog appears, systemd is asking for administrator rights.
svc.criticalWarning: This is a critical unit. Stopping or disabling it can break the system, end your desktop session or lock you out until a reboot.
journal.title: Logs of {name}
journal.error: The journal could not be read.
journal.limited: System logs are visible only to members of the adm or systemd-journal group; you may see only part of them.
journal.foot: {n} entries. New entries appear every few seconds.
alerts.err.name: Give the rule a name (up to 80 characters).
alerts.err.for: The duration must be a whole number of seconds, 0 to 86400.
alerts.err.quietBoth: Quiet hours need both a start and an end.
alerts.err.quietSame: Quiet hours must start and end at different times.
alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.intro: Hearth watches these rules all the time and notifies your desktop once per incident.
alerts.noRules: No rules. Add one to be told when something goes wrong.
alerts.form.name: Name
alerts.form.hysteresis: To avoid flapping, an alert ends only once the value is back past the threshold by {n} {unit}.
alerts.form.quiet: Quiet hours (record, but do not notify)
alerts.form.quietHint: Local time; may span midnight (22:00 to 07:00).
palette.label: Command palette
palette.placeholder: Go to a page, open an app or find a service…
palette.hint: ↑ ↓ to move · Enter to open · Esc to close
disks.title: Disks
disks.intro: How full each disk is, how busy, and what takes the space.
disks.exploreHome: See what takes space in your home
disks.sizesIntro: Measure folders in your home or on disks you own.
disks.measuring: Measuring… {done} of {total} folders ({s} s). Sizes appear as each folder is done.
disks.partial: stopped before the end; sizes are too small
disks.error: The folder could not be measured.
disks.footnote: Sizes are space allocated on disk, like du; hard links count once. Links are not followed and other disks mounted inside a folder are not counted. Disk health (SMART) needs the privileged helper and arrives in phase 2.
docker.title: Docker
docker.intro: Containers on this machine, through hearth-broker.
docker.state.no-broker.title: hearth-broker is not running
docker.state.no-broker.body: Hearth reaches Docker only through its helper, hearth-broker. Install the Hearth package (it sets up hearth-broker.socket) or start it with: sudo systemctl enable --now hearth-broker.socket
docker.state.not-member.title: You are not in the hearth group
docker.state.not-member.body: Only members of the hearth group may use hearth-broker. Add yourself with: sudo adduser $USER hearth — then log out and back in.
docker.state.no-docker.title: Docker is not available
docker.state.no-docker.body: Docker is not installed or not running. Install docker.io (or Docker Engine) and start docker.service.
docker.state.error.title: Docker could not be read
docker.none: No containers yet. Containers you create with docker run or docker compose appear here.
docker.problemBanner: {n} container(s) unhealthy or exited with an error.
docker.col.name: Container
docker.footnote: CPU is a share of one core (200% is two full cores); memory leaves out page cache, like docker stats. Usage is sampled every 2 s while this page is open.
docker.authHint: If a password dialog appears, polkit is asking for permission to change Docker.
docker.confirmBody: This container and its writable layer are deleted. Named volumes are kept.
docker.confirmRunning: It is running: it will be stopped by force first.
detail.envMasked: Values of names containing PASSWORD, TOKEN, KEY or SECRET are hidden by hearth-broker; Hearth never receives them.
detail.risksBody: This container can reach the host beyond Docker's isolation:
detail.stats.none: No usage yet: the container is not running, or the first sample is on its way.
detail.logs.ended: The container stopped; no more output.
detail.logs.foot: {n} line(s), newest at the bottom. Output is shown as plain text.
shell.intro: Opens /bin/sh inside the container. Your administrator password is asked every time.
shell.refused: Hearth does not open a shell in this container: it can reach the host ({why}), so a shell in it would be a root shell on this machine.
reason.inUse: uses this image; it keeps running from it
image.total: {n} image(s), {size} in all (shared layers counted once per image)
image.none: No images yet. Images appear here once you pull or build one.
image.col.name: Image
image.footnote: Size counts every layer of the image; unique is what removing it alone would free (layers no other image uses).
image.pulling: Pulling {name}… this can take a while.
image.confirmBody: This image and all its tags are deleted; layers other images use are kept.
image.confirmInUse: Containers use this image. They keep running, but cannot be re-created from it until it is pulled again.
image.layersIntro: {n} history entries, newest first. Entries of 0 B only changed settings (CMD, ENV, LABEL…).
image.update.intro: Asks each tag's registry which image it serves now and compares it with the one pulled here. Nothing is downloaded.
image.update.untagged: An untagged image has nothing to compare.
image.update.local: built or tagged here: nothing to compare
image.scan.missing: Trivy is not installed. Install it (e.g. from aquasecurity's Debian repository) to scan images for known vulnerabilities.
image.scan.intro: Scans the image's packages with Trivy {version}. The first scan downloads Trivy's database and can take a few minutes.
image.scan.truncated: Only the 500 most severe are listed.
compose.none: No Compose projects. Containers started with docker compose appear here, grouped by project.
compose.reason.gone: the project has no containers any more
compose.footnote: Actions run on the project's existing containers, dependencies first when starting and last when stopping. Changing the compose file, creating or recreating containers is done with docker compose itself.
cleanup.containers.body: Containers that are created, exited or dead. Their writable layer goes; their images and named volumes stay.
cleanup.images.body: Dangling images: old layers left behind when a tag moved to a newer image. Tagged images are never touched here.
cleanup.networks.body: Networks no container is attached to (bridge, host and none are never removed).
cleanup.volumes.body: Volumes no container uses, not even a stopped one. They may hold data (databases, uploads) you still want.
cleanup.build.body: Cached build steps not in use. Builds get slower until the cache fills again.
cleanup.confirmBody: Exactly these are removed; anything created after this preview is left alone:
cleanup.volumesWarning: Volumes hold data. What is in them is deleted for good and cannot be recovered from Hearth.
cleanup.done: Removed {n}; {kept} kept because they are in use again.
cleanup.footnote: Sizes come from Docker and can overlap (a layer shared by two dangling images counts twice). Each removal asks for your password through polkit.
tiles.title: Your services
tiles.empty: No tiles yet. Add the web services you use (a NAS, a media server, a router page) to open them from here and see whether they answer.
tile.name: Name
tile.upload: Or upload one (PNG, WebP or SVG, up to 512 KiB)
tile.healthHint: While this page is open, Hearth asks the address every minute (HEAD or GET, 5 s timeout, at most one redirect on the same host, no passwords or cookies sent).
tile.err.scheme: Start with http:// or https:// followed by a host name or IP address.
tile.err.credentials: Leave out the user name and password; Hearth never sends them.
tile.err.iconSize: The icon is larger than 512 KiB.
tiles.suggestHint: Looks for published container ports and local web servers, and asks each one for its page title. Nothing is added until you save the form.
tiles.suggestNone: No new web services found on this machine.
pkg.title: Packages
pkg.intro: Everything installed on this computer, from every package manager.
pkg.error: The package database could not be read.
pkg.col.name: Package
pkg.tag.autoHint: Installed automatically because another package needs it
pkg.updates.none: Debian packages are up to date.
pkg.updates.error: The updates could not be listed.
pkg.footnote: Debian package changes go through PackageKit, holds through Hearth's helper; both may ask for your password. Run apt update to refresh the update list.
pkg.authHint: If a password dialog appears, the system is asking for administrator rights.
pkg.userHint: Running the package manager's own uninstall as you…
pkg.reason.systemSnap: a snap the system runs on (base, kernel or snapd)
pkg.detail.error: The package details could not be read.
pkg.detail.noRdeps: No installed package depends on it.
tools.title: Tools
tools.intro: Every program you can run from a terminal, and where it came from.
tools.loading: Reading PATH and the package lists…
tools.error: The tools could not be listed.
tools.col.name: Program
tools.tag.shadowsHint: Programs with the same name later in PATH, never run: {paths}
tools.footnote: Versions come from the owning package (or a Go program's build information); Hearth never runs a listed program to find out.
tools.man.title: man {name}
tools.man.none: This program has no manual page.
tools.man.error: The manual page could not be shown.
net.title: Network
net.intro: Who listens on which port, what is connected, and how this machine is on the network.
net.count: {n} listening ports, {exposed} reachable from the network.
net.error: The sockets could not be read.
net.dnsStubHint: Programs ask systemd-resolved on 127.0.0.53, which forwards to these servers.
net.fwHint: Every listening port marked “Exposed” is reachable from your networks.
net.footnote: Other users' ports show their service or container; the exact process is known only for your own.
net.truncated: Only the first 2000 connections are shown.
net.scope.all: Listens on every address: any network this machine is on can reach it.
net.scope.address: Listens on one address: the network of that address can reach it.
net.scope.loopback: Listens on loopback: only programs on this machine can reach it.
net.lineage.title: {proto} port {port}
net.lineage.error: Its origin could not be read.
net.lineage.inexact: The main process of its unit (another user's: the socket's exact holder is not visible to you).
net.lineage.noProcess: Owned by {user}; its process is not visible.
term.newHint: A new shell in your home folder (Ctrl+Shift+T)
